entry_state: Impairment allocation preserves individual floors and a finite residual, while reversal respects the depreciated no-impairment path and excludes goodwill. A zero-weight reversal remains unresolved rather than receiving invented weights. Provisions require an existing duty and supported measurement. The factory case now asks why low output cannot load all idle-capacity cost into its remaining goods.
exit_state: The factory example separates admitted unit cost, unallocated overhead, abnormal waste and cash/noncash resource origins; its low-output cash increase 10 reconciles by two equivalent bridges. The changed-obligation section has begun with restoration: estimate changes depend on cost versus revaluation history, while discount unwind and settlement have distinct effects. Its detailed restoration discussion is still being read.
findings: The production comparison changes output and sales explicitly while retaining the same fixed costs and separately stated accident; it does not imply equal total spending.
Normal capacity, source period, homogeneous cost pool, revenue eligibility and NRV are supplied before the calculation. Zero output receives no invented unit cost.
The cash bridge explains why adding all factory depreciation requires subtracting the full inventory increase; the alternate cash-only bridge gives the same 10.
Restoration distinguishes discount unwind, new estimates and actual settlement and retains an unresolved fact-specific cash classification. No additional confirmed defect.

equation.exposition_role: Mechanism-bearing local normal-capacity allocation for the specified cost pool.
equation.symbols_units_domain: Q is positive completed units; f and u are currency per unit; U is currency expense; 100 is normal units and 180 fixed currency cost.
equation.assumptions_timing: Constant homogeneous pool, direct/variable cost 4 per unit, supported normal capacity and no opening/WIP stock.
equation.source_and_equality: Correct scoped construction: f=180/max(100,Q), u=4+f, U=180-Qf; not a universal multi-product formula.
equation.interpretation: Low output leaves expense; high output caps total allocation at 180. With no output all 180 is expense.
equation.transition: The table varies both output and sales and then reconciles the cost and cash populations.
